extraction.name: ACL OCL
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. It includes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to Semantic Scholar, spanning papers published from 1952 to September 2022.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi; Yanxia Qin; Benjamin Aw; Niranjana Unnithan; Min-Yen Kan
extraction.citeAs: Rohatgi, Shaurya; Qin, Yanxia; Aw, Benjamin; Unnithan, Niranjana; Kan, Min-Yen. 2023. The ACL OCL Corpus: Advancing Open Science in Computational Linguistics.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The corpus was constructed by crawling PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology website, removing PDF files longer than 50 pages, extracting structured full text from PDFs using GROBID, extracting figures and tables using PDFFigures, and enriching papers with additional information from the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph via its Graph API. The dataset undergoes annual updates by identifying newly added ACL Anthology papers through URL changes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Web API, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Certain fields are only valid for a portion of papers. For example, only 16.8% of OCL papers have arXiv_paper_id, indicating a corresponding version in arXiv.org. The paper also reports extraction failures and missing content in full-text quality assessment, including missing sections, missing footnotes, undetected figures, and undetected or incorrectly detected tables.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources are PDF documents and metadata from the ACL Anthology website, plus additional metadata and citation information from the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph Graph API.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors removed PDF files longer than 50 pages, which were mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks. They linked ACL Anthology papers to Semantic Scholar records and added automatically detected fields such as language and predicted_topic.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF files were processed with GROBID for full-text extraction into an S2ORC-JSON schema including metadata, authors, body text, citations, references, and sections. Figures and tables were extracted from PDFs using PDFFigures and stored separately from textual data. Language was detected using a public language detection toolkit with title and abstract as inputs. The dataset is provided in CSV and Apache Parquet formats.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The corpus itself is largely unlabeled, but model-predicted silver topic labels are included. For topic classification, the authors created a scientific topic dataset (STop) by crawling published papers from ACL 2020, EMNLP 2020, ACL-IJCNLP 2021, EACL 2021, and NAACL 2021 together with their topic labels from conference websites, aligning those papers with ACL OCL, and using the resulting 2,545 documents with 21 topics as training and testing data. Topic labels originate from conference submission topics.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors used 5-fold cross-validation for topic classification experiments, with 80% training and 20% test splits balanced by topic. They compared zero-shot, semi-supervised, keyword-based, and PLM-based methods using Macro F1, Weighted F1, and Accuracy. They note that predicted topics are silver data and discuss errors due to insufficient training samples and topic overlap.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: BART-large-MNLI; TF-IDF; YAKE!; SciBERT; SPECTER; langdetect
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates by downloading and processing papers recently added to the ACL Anthology, identified by monitoring URL changes. The authors state they plan to update OCL by year to keep it alive and aim to keep it up-to-date with ACL Anthology data.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: author names; publication venue address; language written in
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The corpus is intended to advance open scientific research in computational linguistics, accelerate scientific progress, and promote reproducibility by providing accessible and standardized data resources. The authors highlight that it can benefit a wide range of research tasks and enable analyses such as temporal topic trends, historical language change, and knowledge graph construction.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The corpus focuses only on peer-reviewed and open-access computational linguistics papers from the ACL Anthology, so it is not comprehensive beyond that source. English is the dominant language in the corpus, and prior work cited by the authors notes underrepresentation of many low-resource languages. The authors also note bias in the distribution of top-cited papers toward dominant topics such as machine translation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The corpus is small-scale relative to broader scholarly corpora and only includes peer-reviewed, open-access CL papers from the ACL Anthology. It does not include other sources beyond ACL Anthology. Full-text quality is limited by PDF extraction errors, including incorrect metadata, missing section names, merged paragraphs, footnotes mixed with text, misidentified captions, and poor extraction of tables, figures, and in-line equations. The corpus is also largely unlabeled for task-specific annotations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as an open scholarly corpus for a wide range of research applications, including metadata analysis, bibliographic research, document-level information extraction, section-wise tasks such as related work generation, multimodal research with figures, citation and knowledge graph analysis, topic trend analysis, emerging topic detection, paper-reviewer matching, terminology detection, coreference resolution, pre-training or fine-tuning scientific language models, scientific assistants, summarization, contribution extraction, future work prediction, historical language change analysis, and intelligent academic search.
